name: NJM8830 / NJM8830GM1
tagline: Nisshinbo's 2022 low-voltage audio dual: 0.000012% THD, 2.5 nV/√Hz and 100 mA output for headphone and DAC stages.

lineage.note: Sole source. Production announced 2022-06-07; NJM prefix inherited from New Japan Radio (NJR).

part_numbers.note: Family name; HSOP8-M1 and DFN8-W1 (ESON8-W1). DFN8 orderable suffix unconfirmed.
HSOP8-M1; -TE1 is tape-and-reel (LCSC C19941438). Akizuki g117507, DIP8 kit g118285.

reputation.summary: A 2022 launch covered by PHILE WEB, Nikkan Kogyo and PR Times, sold to hobbyists by Akizuki with a DIP8 adapter. Japanese swappers report strong results. diyAudio bench posts show it beating the OPA1642A but not the OPA1612A, with low overshoot and fast settling. Seen as an IEM or low-impedance headphone driver.
typical_uses: Preamp and active-filter stages on low-voltage rails
DAC output / buffer stages in 5 V-class gear
Op-amp rolling via Akizuki HSOP8-to-DIP8 adapter
caveats: Max supply is only ±5.25 V (10.5 V total); never fit it in ±12 V or ±15 V sockets.
SMD only (HSOP8-M1 / DFN8-W1); socket swaps need an adapter board.
About 6–6.5 mA supply current; a diyAudio poster calls it unsuitable for portable gear.
90 MHz GBW: adapter installs need short, well-decoupled layouts to stay stable.
Praise is mostly Japanese anecdote plus one diyAudio thread, where it measured below the OPA1612A.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit reports. Recent single-source part sold via Mouser, LCSC and Akizuki. It has no DIP package, so any 'DIP-8 NJM8830' is an adapter board (such as Akizuki's kit) or a fake.
